title: Concurrent activations can leave multiple manual covers active

evidence.quote:
current_active = session.exec(
        select(ManualCover).where(ManualCover.is_active == True)
    ).all()
...
    cover.is_active = True
...
    session.commit()

reasoning: The route reads the currently active rows, deactivates only that snapshot, then marks the requested cover active. If two requests activate different inactive covers concurrently, both can read the same old active cover before either commits. Each request then deactivates only the old cover and activates its own target, so both newly requested covers can remain active. Downstream code that selects the first active cover will then behave nondeterministically.
reproduction: Start with cover A active and covers B/C inactive. Send concurrent POST requests to /covers/{B}/activate and /covers/{C}/activate so both read current_active before either commit. After both commits, B and C can both have is_active=true.
recommendation: Make activation atomic. For example, execute a single transactional UPDATE that sets is_active based on the target id for all manual_covers, or add an application-level write lock/DB uniqueness guarantee so only one row can be active at commit time.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The inspected test flow activates covers sequentially and only asserts the normal single-request path; it does not exercise concurrent activation or stale active-row snapshots.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test that creates three covers, runs two activations for different covers with controlled interleaving or concurrent clients, and asserts exactly one ManualCover row remains active after both requests complete.
minimumFixScope: Change activate_manual_cover to update all ManualCover rows in one transaction/statement, and add a concurrency regression test for simultaneous activations.
